angle_en: A ladder of higher and higher layers
angle_hi: ऊपर की ओर जाने वाली सीढ़ी

en.intro: Krishna asks which enemy is hardest to conquer, and answers by mapping the inner layers. Listen for the ladder that leads upward.
en.notice: The word parah means higher than the one below, and Krishna builds a ladder with it. The senses are higher than the body, the mind is higher than the senses, the discerning mind is higher than the mind, and the self is higher than the discerning mind.
en.next: Krishna now tells Arjuna to use this knowledge to steady the self and destroy desire.
en.meaning: The senses are higher than the body; the mind is higher than the senses; the discerning mind is higher than the mind. And beyond the discerning mind is the self.

hi.intro: कृष्ण पूछते हैं कि कौन सा शत्रु सबसे कठिन है, और उत्तर में एक सीढ़ी बताते हैं। ऊपर की ओर जाने वाली इस सीढ़ी को ध्यान से सुनिए।
hi.meaning: इंद्रियों को शरीर से श्रेष्ठ और सूक्ष्म कहा गया है, इंद्रियों से श्रेष्ठ मन है और मन से श्रेष्ठ बुद्धि। और जो बुद्धि से भी परे है, वह आत्मा है।
hi.notice: परा शब्द का अर्थ है नीचे वाले से ऊँचा, और कृष्ण इसके साथ एक सीढ़ी बनाते हैं। शरीर से ऊँची इन्द्रियाँ, इन्द्रियों से ऊँचा मन, मन से ऊँची बुद्धि, और बुद्धि से भी ऊँची आत्मा।
hi.next: कृष्ण अब अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि इस ज्ञान से अपने आप को स्थिर करो और काम रूपी शत्रु का नाश करो।

issues: meaning_changed: "जो बुद्धि से भी परे है, वह आत्मा है।" (The Hindi meaning states 'And that which is beyond the intellect is the self (soul)', whereas the fixed English meaning and the source verse explicitly state 'Beyond the discerning mind is the self'. The Hindi translation drops 'discerning' (बुद्धि) and replaces it with 'intellect' (बुद्धि), but more critically, it changes the subject from 'the self' to 'desire (काम)', which directly contradicts the previous verses and the standard interpretation (as noted in the source context where Gita Press's Swami Ramsukhdas interprets 'सः' as desire, but Shankaracharya and Madhusudana Sarasvati take it as the Self). This is a severe contradiction of the verse's core meaning.)

meaning_changed: "जो बुद्धि से भी परे है, वह आत्मा है" (The Hindi meaning drops the hierarchy of 'the discerning mind is higher than the mind' and incorrectly presents 'the self' as the only thing beyond the intellect, missing the intermediate layer of 'the discerning mind' (बुद्धि) being higher than the mind (मन). Additionally, it contradicts the SOURCE's explicit statement that the self (सः) is beyond the intellect, as the Bhagavad Gita uses 'सः' to refer to the Self (Atman), not 'desire' (काम) as the Gita Press translation mentioned in the context might suggest.)

meaning_changed: "और जो बुद्धि से भी परे है, वह काम है" (This Hindi phrase incorrectly states that what is beyond the intellect is 'काम' (desire). The source explicitly says it is the 'self' (आत्मा/सः), and the English meaning also confirms 'the self'. This contradicts the core teaching of the verse.)

meaning_changed: "जो बुद्धि से भी परे है, वह आत्मा है" (The source verse says 'यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः' (and beyond the discerning mind is the self). The Hindi translation in the script changes this to 'जो बुद्धि से भी परे है, वह आत्मा है' (and what is beyond the intellect, that is the self). This is a severe meaning change because it alters the grammatical structure of the Sanskrit (which says 'that which is beyond the intellect, that is it/the self') and incorrectly inserts the word 'आत्मा' (soul/self) into the translation of the second line. The correct meaning should be 'and beyond the discerning mind is the self/that' (and beyond the discerning mind is that), not 'and what is beyond the intellect is the self'. Also, the English meaning provided in the script is correct and does not match the Hindi translation's addition of 'आत्मा'. Furthermore, the Hindi translation incorrectly translates 'सः' as 'काम' (desire) in the first line, whereas the source verse does not mention desire here. The source Insight/Detail correctly identifies the self as being beyond the intellect, but the Hindi translation provided in the script is severely flawed.)

meaning_changed: "और जो बुद्धि से भी पर है, वह काम है" (The source verse says 'मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिः' (but the discerning mind is higher than the mind) and 'यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः' (and beyond the discerning mind is the self). The Hindi translation in the script says 'मन से भी पर बुद्धि है और जो बुद्धि से भी पर है, वह काम है' (and beyond the mind is the intellect and what is beyond the intellect is desire). This is a severe meaning change because it incorrectly identifies 'सः' (that/the self) as 'काम' (desire). The source verse does not mention desire in this verse. The previous verse (41) mentions desire as the enemy, but this verse (42) is about the hierarchy of the self, mind, and intellect.)

wrong_fact: "और जो बुद्धि से भी पर है, वह काम है" (The source verse says 'यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः' (and beyond the discerning mind is the self). The Hindi translation in the script says 'और जो बुद्धि से भी पर है, वह काम है' (and what is beyond the intellect is desire). This is a wrong fact because it incorrectly identifies 'सः' as 'काम' (desire) instead of the self. The source verse does not mention desire in this verse.)
